source.title: How Fragile Is On-Device Language Model Safety? Localizing Safety-Critical Parameters for Sparse Fault Analysis

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether safety-targeted weight modifications can increase harmful-prompt attack success, using low-rank and parameter-level localization methods rather than the original single residual-stream direction method.
record.gate_note: The paper does not measure or remove the original difference-in-means residual-stream direction. It reports harmful-prompt ASR after weight modifications, relevant to V2. Utility results are recorded as findings about the broader claim but are not direct tests of V2. Related-work findings cited from other studies are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: The study does not test or use the refusal direction. It applies Wei et al. (2024) safety–utility localization to LLaMA-2-7B-Chat: SVD-based low-rank weight components and activation-aware set-difference pruning. It then reports harmful-prompt ASR and tinyBenchmarks accuracy. No difference-in-means harmful-minus-harmless direction is computed, ablated, added or turned into a weight edit, and nothing is compared against it. Arditi et al. appears only in related work. V2 names abliteration, a weight edit of that specific direction. These are different weight interventions, so the ASR results do not bear on V2 or any other version. They are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that safety-sensitive parameters are concentrated, mainly in down_proj. Pruning 0.19% of weights gives 53% Basic and 56% GCG ASR with near-baseline utility. They present this as a reduced candidate space for future bit-level fault analysis, not as a demonstrated hardware attack.
record.recipe_differences: Uses module-output SVD for a utility-orthogonalized safety-associated weight component and an activation-aware safety-versus-utility parameter ranking, then removes or prunes weights. It does not use the original difference-in-means residual-stream direction, project it out at every layer and position, or add it. The paper presents weight interventions, not a physical fault attack.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies with intervention scope and retained fraction: Table 1 reports different ASRs for all modules, MLP only, and down_proj, and across retained fractions. Table 2 reports different ASRs for target component and selected weight fraction. Basic and GCG results also differ.

fits_no_version.finding: On LLaMA-2-7B-Chat, Wei-style low-rank safety-component removal and safety-specific pruning raise refusal-pattern-based ASR. Values: 87%/98% with all modules and the full component; 53%/56% when pruning 0.19% of weights in down_proj; 20%/14% with o_proj only. ASR falls as the edit is sparsified or localized. The unmodified ASR is not reported.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Safety-specific weights localized by safety–utility attribution, concentrated in MLP down_proj, can be removed by sparse weight edits to degrade refusal, separately from the refusal-direction account.

fits_no_version.finding: tinyBenchmarks accuracy stays near the 52.2% baseline for localized edits (51.2–52.0%). It drops for broad edits (47.1% for all-module pruning).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sparse safety-localized weight edits largely preserve measured utility, while broader edits cost more.

record.peer_reviewed: NeurIPS 2026 Workshop: SLMs for Agentic Systems
record.problems: Only one model is tested. The paper does not report unmodified-model Basic or GCG ASR, statistical uncertainty, or random and magnitude-based intervention baselines; it says such baselines are future work. tinyBenchmarks is described as a compact estimate of utility. The interventions simulate parameter modifications and do not demonstrate physical bit faults.
record.rows_left_out: None of the reported Table 1 or Table 2 outcome values were omitted. Related-work results cited from other papers and calibration data used to construct the interventions are not rows.

untested.parts: No weight edit of the difference-in-means refusal direction (abliteration) is performed. Only Wei et al.-style low-rank and pruning edits on LLaMA-2-7B-Chat are tested.
No difference-in-means direction is extracted, ablated or added.
The low-rank safety subspaces are not compared with single-direction, affine or cone accounts.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V2 link was wrong. V2 concerns abliteration of the difference-in-means direction, and this paper uses Wei et al. (2024) localization methods instead. The paper also lacks an unmodified-model ASR, random or magnitude baselines, and uncertainty, and it tests only one model. The reader's limits_scope label was based on ASR below 100%, which is not evidence about V2 anyway.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test a single harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means residual-stream direction, its removal at every layer and position, adding it to induce refusal, or the associated capability claim.

Uses low-rank safety-associated weight removal and parameter pruning, not a weight edit of the original difference-in-means refusal direction. It reports ASR rather than a direct refusal-rate measure and tests only LLaMA-2-7B-Chat.
Does not test attacks suppressing the claimed direction or training against its ablation.
Does not compare affine, cone, or multiple-direction accounts of refusal.
Does not separate harmfulness judgments from refusal decisions.
Does not test transfer across languages, model variants, or base and instruct models.
Does not vary refusal-training methods or stages.

relation.reason: The only mention is one Related Work sentence saying refusal can be mediated by a low-dimensional residual-stream direction. The direction is not used, tested or discussed further.

tranche.reason: Arditi et al. is cited once in Related Work. The method follows Wei et al. 2024 (module-output SVD and activation-aware set-difference pruning). No difference-in-means direction is computed, ablated or added, and no version is tested.

source_check.notes: Single model (LLaMA-2-7B-Chat). ASR comes from refusal-keyword matching on 100 AdvBench prompts. The paper gives no ASR for the unmodified model, no random or magnitude baselines (left to future work) and no uncertainty. The 7 utility rows still carry observed/partial states, while the ASR rows were fixed to cannot_determine. They should be made consistent (cannot_determine), since all rows are linked to no version.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Tested low-rank and parameter-pruning weight interventions on LLaMA-2-7B-Chat
reader_labels.reason: All reported Basic and GCG ASRs are below complete attack success, so the weight modifications produce partial rather than complete removal of refusal-pattern responses (rows L-All-1-Basic through P-o-GCG). The unmodified-model ASR is not reported.
